author: potuz
content: While I mostly agree that we should increase DA space given that we have the technology now to handle it. I believe otoh that we should now stop doing this for free. A higher and meaningful minimum blob gas price is already in order

author: trent_vanepps
content:
> I believe otoh that we should now stop doing this for free.

not sure this follows - should we not increase the gas limit in Glamsterdam because mainnet base fee is ~1gwei?

your statements outline a very different approach to protocol decisions than what we've done in the past (to my knowledge), which is to only set floors/min fees when a resource needs to be better priced for safety reasons (calldata 7623, blob reserve 7918) or purely left to floating markets (1559 base fee)

this new approach needs to be very well reasoned if it will be justified!

author: derekchiang
content: yeah i also personally feel (not a shared Ethlabs opinion yet) that we should enforce a minimum blob fee, since Ethereum DA does have some pricing powers over the users who actually need it (e.g. Base/Arbitrum).  however this would open a can of worms where the ACD is now tasked with making economic/business decisions for Ethereum, which is a tricky road to go down

author: potuz
content:
> should we not increase the gas limit in Glamsterdam because mainnet base fee is ~1gwei?
No, this is really different. In fact the lack of a reasonable minimum fee actually hurts rollups because when there is actually contention then fees spike up at a rythm that is so slow because of the lack of a minimum that it becomes a priority gas auction, an auction even against the opportunity cost of **not including** the blob that gives the builder/proposer extra time to get a better bid for MEV extraction. This cycle feeds itself: rollups can't estimate this extra fee correctly on time (specially if you want to charge in a trustless manner also in L2) to which builders end up not including as many blobs as they could since it's rational to do so as they are therefore able to submit later bids for a more profitable block, which makes the data base fee stay low at a not meaningful price. 

This makes blob data price behave in a bimodal order in which in normal operation the protocol gets nothing because rollups pay nothing and in congestion the protocol gets nothing because proposers are getting everything in the form of priority. It is literally a lose-lose situation for L1 **and** L2s. For L2s it would be much better to have a higher base fee and a predictable gas model for their users instead of absurd spikes when they need to be included in congestion.
